name: Healthpeak Properties, Inc.
sector: Real Estate — Healthcare REIT (outpatient medical, lab / life science, senior housing)
moat_justification: Weak-moderate REIT moat: scarce on-/near-campus outpatient medical locations, long health-system relationships and post-merger scale are real but replicable with capital, and there is no pricing power beyond contractual rent escalators. The measured record argues against a higher score: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is null for every year (the filer tags no operating-income line the proxy needs), gross margin ran 58.1–60.2% in FY2021–24 with no expansion, OE/share fell from $1.57 in FY2016 to $0.49 in FY2025, Q2 2026 FFO as Adjusted was flat year over year at $0.46, and lab occupancy is only 78.5% with same-store lab NOI down 3.2% — a franchise earning well below a wide-moat standard through the cycle.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 8.9%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 28.6x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Diversified healthcare REIT, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% on any basis: Tier D, weighted IRR 4.90%, weighted IV@15% $3.66 vs $18.98 on the engine OE base (which charges all development capex), and even on the REIT-native AFFO basis (~$1.69/sh in FY2025 per external reporting, a ~6.4% dividend yield plus ~0–2% per-share growth) the expected return is high-single-digit; it would clear 15% only at the engine hurdle price of $3.66, which the sector model misfit makes a model artifact rather than a real entry point — confidence low.
moat_for: Scarce healthcare locations: outpatient medical buildings on/near hospital campuses and lab clusters in core life-science markets are supply-constrained and slow to replicate

Health-system relationships and scale: the March 2024 Physicians Realty Trust merger made it one of the largest outpatient medical landlords; Q2 2026 executed 1.6M sq ft of new/renewal leases with outpatient occupancy 90.7%
Long leases with contractual escalators and diversified rent roll across outpatient medical, lab and senior housing (Janus Living revenue +45% YoY in Q2 2026)
Investment-grade balance sheet (BBB+/Baa1 per Q2 2026 reporting) with net debt / adjusted EBITDAre 4.7x at Q2 2026 and demonstrated capital-recycling access ($1.025B Brookfield outpatient JV recap)
moat_against: No structural pricing power: rent is set by local market supply/demand at renewal; tenants can relocate and competing landlords/developers can add supply with commodity capital
Lab / life-science oversupply: lab occupancy 78.5% and same-store lab NOI -3.2% YoY in Q2 2026; recovery depends on biotech funding, not on Healthpeak

Weak through-cycle per-share record: OE/share $1.57 (FY2016) to $0.49 (FY2025), FFO as Adjusted flat YoY in Q2 2026, dividend cut in FY2021 (fundamentals.json last_cut_fy 2021; DPS TTM $1.22 vs $2.10 in FY2016)
Leverage and rate exposure: net debt $9.38B is 28.6x normalized OE on the engine basis; REIT cash flows are hostage to cap rates and refinancing costs
